Ranked!

The minerals are useful, but absorption is not perfectly straightforward. Tree-nut allergy limits use. For some people, almonds are simply not a usable option.

episode.narrationText:
Zucchini!
-
Ranked!
-
0.3 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 0.1 grams, supporting a better fat profile. Omega 3 is 15 milligrams, a weak mark for vegetables.
-
3.1 grams of carbs. Glycemic index is 15 GI, supporting better carb quality. Fibre is 1 gram, a small miss for vegetables.
-
1.2 grams of protein. Not enough to make protein a serious strength.
-
Vitamin C is 20% daily value, useful for collagen formation and antioxidant support. Vitamin A is only 4% daily value, a weak mark for vegetables.
-
Potassium is 6% daily value, useful for fluid balance. Calcium is only 1% daily value, a weak mark for vegetables.
-
Pros first: good volume for the calories. That matters for satiety and general usefulness. Helps add volume without much calorie cost. That makes vegetables easier to use often. Easy to build meals around. A practical plus because good foods need realistic use cases.
-
Cons next: texture or flavour can limit repeat use. Strong nutrition still has to survive normal eating habits. Prep can decide whether it actually gets eaten. Vegetables can lose practical value when washing, chopping, or cooking becomes a barrier. Very light profile can feel underpowered. For some vegetables, the practical payoff is more volume and texture than a big nutrient payload.
-
Big strengths are carb quality and good volume for the calories, but the biggest weaknesses are texture or flavour can limit repeat use and prep can decide whether it actually gets eaten.
